clue.text: Regime seeing annihilation of middle class as key again

indicators.note: the middle of the word regime is wiped out, leaving only its two outer letters

parts.note: a class is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A political regime purges its middle classes.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing EGIM, the middle of REGIME, leaves RE; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype a document is to key it in a second time on a keyboard.

clue.text: Regretted vulgar sounds

indicators.note: sounds tells us the word for vulgar is said aloud, not written

parts.note: vulgar means rude

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for having made crude noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Rued is the past tense of rue, an old word for regret or be sorry about.

clue.text: Might an East End trichologist treat this for nothing?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker from London's East End drops the H at the start of words, so the phrase is pronounced that way

parts.note: a trichologist is a hair and scalp specialist, so a patient might bring thin hair

explanation.surface: A wry question about what a London hair specialist might treat without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End of London is Cockney country, where speakers drop their aitches: thin hair comes out as 'thin 'air'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made out of thin air comes from nothing at all, so the phrase stands for nothingness.

clue.text: Stop that manic panic about stuff!

indicators.note: about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the other piece
manic means frenzied, so the letters of panic are thrown about

parts.note: stuff, as in gear or belongings, is kit

explanation.surface: Someone tells a frantic person to calm down about their things.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'stuff' as a verb, but here it is a noun meaning gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack it in is an informal British command meaning quit or give up doing something.

clue.text: Prohibition of smacking's good and right

parts.note: smacking is a slap
a prohibition is a ban

explanation.surface: Banning the smacking of children is good and proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prohibition of smacking' gives BAN of SLAP, written in answer order as SLAP BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-bang means exactly or directly, as in slap-bang in the middle, much like right in the middle.

clue.text: Generous — and inclined to be magnanimous

parts.note: a magnanimous, big-hearted person is large in spirit
to be inclined to do something is to be minded to do it

explanation.surface: A description of a generous, big-hearted person.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-minded means broad and tolerant in outlook, a big-hearted generosity of spirit.

clue.text: Turns from small to big noise during escalation

indicators.note: escalation means going up, and in a down clue going up means reading backwards

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
taken as written
a big noise is an important person, a VIP

explanation.surface: Things turn from small matters into loud noise as a quarrel escalates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; S TO VIP reads upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to turn on a central point, so pivots and turns are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Unemotional principals in Faust were sacked

indicators.note: the principals of words are their leading letters, the first ones
sacked means dismissed, so those leading letters are thrown out

explanation.surface: The lead actors in a production of Faust were fired.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping F and W, the first letters of Faust and were, leaves AUST and ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern and severe in manner, without warmth or feeling.

clue.text: Garbo doesn't have time to tease relative

indicators.note: doesn't have means the film star's first name goes without one letter

parts.note: Greta Garbo was the Swedish-born film star
to tease is to taunt

explanation.surface: Greta Garbo, who wanted to be alone, has no time to tease a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tease' supplies the whole second word; 'Garbo' points to the actress by surname only.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt is a parent's aunt, a family relative two generations up.

clue.text: Show electronic cable?

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
Vince Cable was a leading Liberal Democrat politician

explanation.surface: A question about showing someone an electronic cable.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C of 'Cable' is hidden at the start of the clue; Sir Vince Cable was a UK Business Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or reveal a feeling or quality clearly.

clue.text: Father Jack, perhaps, embraced by Anglicans, causing split

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the father and jack go within the Anglicans

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, whose members are Anglicans
a priest is addressed as Father, and Rev is short for Reverend
a jack is a male donkey, and a donkey is an ass

explanation.surface: Father Jack, the drunken priest of the sitcom Father Ted, causes a split among Anglicans.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Jack is the foul-mouthed old priest in the TV comedy Father Ted; here the name is taken apart into a clergyman and a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack or split in a glacier.

clue.text: Joe Bloggs entertains them in variety

indicators.note: in variety means arranged in a different, varied way

explanation.surface: An ordinary chap puts on a show for them at the variety theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' looks like the verb linking two parts, but it is half of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Bloggs is the British name for an imaginary ordinary person, the typical average citizen.

clue.text: Pounding ingredients

indicators.note: pounding means beating, so the letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook beats the meat for a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: beating meat ingredients is what tenderising does.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderising meat is done by pounding it with a mallet before cooking.

clue.text: I'd a way to help poorer countries

parts.note: the letters of the word aid, rearranged or made foreign, read as these clue words

explanation.surface: Someone says they had a way to help developing nations.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: FOREIGN is an anagram indicator acting on AID, which produces I'D A.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign aid is money and help that rich nations give to developing ones.

clue.text: French-Belgian compromise, easily broken

indicators.note: to compromise something is to damage or disorder it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: France and Belgium reach a fragile compromise.
explanation.definitionFit: Frangible is a formal word for brittle or fragile.

clue.text: List some prime numbers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone lists a few of the prime numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list of dishes or of options to choose from.

clue.text: Engorged lower half of wildebeest upset another wildebeest

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower half of a word is its second half
upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: a gnu is another name for a wildebeest

explanation.surface: An animal story about one wildebeest overturning another.
explanation.walkthrough: The last five letters of WILDEBEEST give BEEST; GNU upset gives UNG.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee-stung lip is full and swollen, as if puffed up by a sting.

clue.text: He helps virgin to shed clothes

indicators.note: shedding clothes means losing the outer layers, so the outside letters go

parts.note: a maiden is a virgin

explanation.surface: A man helps a virgin to undress.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIDEN without its outer letters M and N leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant, someone who helps an official.

clue.text: Tiny amount of petrol mistakenly offered at under a dollar

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so the jumbled letters follow

parts.note: D is short for dollar

indicators.note: mistakenly means wrongly, so the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Petrol mistakenly sold for less than a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offered at' and 'a' are link words; PETROL rearranged gives ROPLET, set under D.
explanation.definitionFit: A droplet is a very small drop of liquid, a tiny quantity.

clue.text: It's very hard to bear Spooner's married lady friend

indicators.note: Spooner's means the first sounds of the two words are swapped, as Rev. Spooner did

parts.note: married means wed
a lady friend is a date

explanation.surface: A man finds his married girlfriend hard to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: WED DATE with first sounds swapped is 'ded wait'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead weight is a heavy, inert load, and figuratively a burden that is hard to carry.

clue.text: Getting dressed, kid goes over to Crosby

indicators.note: goes over means turned over, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: to kid someone is to rag or tease them
Bing Crosby was the American crooner

explanation.surface: A child is dressed up to visit Bing Crosby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; RAG turned over gives GAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbing means clothing oneself, from garb, meaning clothes.

clue.text: Goddess later giving up booze?

indicators.note: giving is read as the later word being given into the middle of the other

parts.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, AA, helps people give up booze
later means then

explanation.surface: A goddess who later swears off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up booze?' with its question mark points to the fellowship Alcoholics Anonymous rather than describing the goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena was the Greek goddess of wisdom, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Waste ground next to railway? It's increasingly profitable

parts.note: to waste away is to grow thin
ground, as in ground down to powder, is dust

explanation.surface: Waste ground beside a railway line turns out to be a money-spinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste ground' looks like one thing, but it is two: 'waste' as a verb and 'ground' as a past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: A growth industry is a sector of the economy expanding and becoming more lucrative.

clue.text: Ocean's water departed on a rising tide?

definitions.note: the definition is ocean; the 's stands for is, linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: a rising tide goes up, and in a down clue going up means reading backwards

parts.note: to pass water is to pee
D is the abbreviation for departed, as in timetables

explanation.surface: Ocean water leaves as the tide comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic name for the sea.

clue.text: News broadcast shot at home

parts.note: a shot fired from a gun is a bullet
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A news report of a shooting at someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short news report on radio or television.

clue.text: Mature bulb regularly coming into flower

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so the picked letters go inside the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Nile

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter

explanation.surface: A bulb grows into a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom: it is a thing that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubile describes a young woman who is mature enough to be marriageable.

clue.text: Alienate Argentines, dropping in unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests a surprising new order for the letters
dropping means leaving out, so these two letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone alienates Argentinians by visiting without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping in' looks like an unexpected visit, but 'dropping' removes IN from ARGENTINES, and the rest, ARGENTES, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to make them hostile or distant, to alienate them.

clue.text: Heartlessly asking boy about potential source of misunderstanding

indicators.note: heartlessly means with the inside removed, keeping only the ends
about means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: A boy is questioned heartlessly about something.
explanation.walkthrough: AG is the outside of ASKING; PAGE turned about gives EGAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A big age difference between people can lead to misunderstanding between generations.
